title: Kohli Is Back, Jaiswal Is Out, and India Have Named Their ODI Squad for England
excerpt: Shubman Gill leads a 15-member squad for the three-match series starting July 14 — with Virat Kohli's return squeezing out the man who scored a century in his absence
body:
India's selectors have made their biggest call of the English summer: Virat Kohli is back in the ODI squad for the three-match series against England, and Yashasvi Jaiswal — the man who scored a century in the third ODI against Afghanistan to make the most of his chance — is the one making way.

Shubman Gill will captain the side, with Shreyas Iyer named vice-captain. The series begins at Edgbaston on July 14, moves to Sophia Gardens in Cardiff on July 16, and concludes at Lord's on July 19 — three matches that will serve as a critical rehearsal for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.

## Kohli's Road Back

Kohli suffered a hamstring injury during the IPL 2026 final, where he played through the pain to hit an unbeaten 75 off 42 balls and guide Royal Challengers Bengaluru to the title. The injury ruled him out of the Afghanistan ODIs, but the 37-year-old has been recovering in London, working closely with Dr. Dinshaw Pardiwalla, the BCCI's chief orthopedic consultant.

He has already cleared a fitness assessment at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. His participation remains officially "subject to fitness," but all indications suggest he will be available. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar had earlier said: "It looks like he might be fit for that England one-day series."

Earlier this year, Kohli had scored 240 runs in a three-ODI home series against New Zealand, averaging 80 with a century and a fifty. In the IPL, he became the first player to cross 9,000 career runs, finishing with 675 runs in 16 matches at an average of 48.50 and a strike rate of 237.31. The hunger, clearly, is not fading.

## The Jaiswal Question

The most contentious part of the squad is who it leaves out. Yashasvi Jaiswal was called up as Kohli's replacement for the Afghanistan series and responded with a century in the third ODI. AB de Villiers, speaking on his YouTube channel, summed up the awkwardness: "It's just a little bit harsh on players sometimes when your King comes back."

Jaiswal remains very much in India's plans — he is expected to feature in the T20I squad against England. But the message from the selectors is clear: when a player of Kohli's stature is available, he walks back in.

## The Full Squad

Shubman Gill (C), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli*, Shreyas Iyer (VC), KL Rahul (WK), Ishan Kishan (WK), Washington Sundar, Axar Patel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar.

*Subject to fitness

The biggest addition beyond Kohli is the return of Jasprit Bumrah, who replaces Prince Yadav. The pace attack now features Bumrah alongside Harshit Rana, Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh, and Prasidh Krishna — a fearsome group for English conditions.

Gurnoor Brar earned his place after impressing during the Afghanistan tour. Harsh Dubey, who took four wickets in two matches against Afghanistan, misses out. The spin department features Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, and Washington Sundar, while Nitish Kumar Reddy adds balance as a pace-bowling all-rounder.

## Why This Series Matters

Gill enjoyed a successful start to his ODI captaincy, leading India to a 3-0 sweep over Afghanistan. But England at home is a different beast entirely. India's record in ODI series in England has been mixed, and with the 2027 World Cup in South Africa looming, these three matches are as much about answering tactical questions as winning them.

Can Gill and Rohit co-exist at the top? Where does Kohli slot in — three or four? Is Bumrah ready for the rigours of a three-format tour after workload management? These are the questions the series will answer.

## The Schedule

- **1st ODI**: July 14, Edgbaston, Birmingham
- **2nd ODI**: July 16, Sophia Gardens, Cardiff
- **3rd ODI**: July 19, Lord's, London

Before the ODIs, India will first play a five-match T20I series against England from July 1, with Shreyas Iyer leading that squad. The T20I side includes 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who continues to make history at every level — he recently smashed an 11-ball fifty for India A against Sri Lanka A, the fastest half-century in List A cricket history.

## The Diaspora Angle

For the estimated 1.9 million Indians and people of Indian origin living in the UK, the summer is stacked. Between the T20Is, ODIs, and the Test series to follow, India will be playing cricket in England for the better part of two months. Tickets for the Lord's ODI are already in high demand — and with Kohli confirmed, expect Edgbaston and Cardiff to follow.

The series also comes during peak summer travel season, with many NRI families planning UK visits that overlap with the cricket. For the diaspora, watching Kohli bat at Lord's — possibly for one of the last times in ODI cricket — carries the weight of a pilgrimage.

*Sources: BCCI, CricTracker, Times of India, Cricket Addictor*
